html:
The Deluge was the invasion of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth by Sweden in 1655, on top of a Russian invasion the year before, which overran most of the country until 1660.

Many nobles at first went over to the Swedish king Charles X Gustav. The defence of the Jasna Góra monastery at Częstochowa in late 1655 became a turning point and a symbol of faith, and a national rising pushed the Swedes out. The Treaty of Oliva of 1660 ended the war, but the Commonwealth lost perhaps a quarter or more of its people to war, plague and hunger, and its towns were looted. It never fully recovered its power. Henryk Sienkiewicz's novel The Deluge, of 1886, made the name famous. Russia kept Kyiv in the wars of those years, and Prussia won full independence.
sum: The Deluge was the invasion of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth by Sweden in 1655, on top of a Russian invasion the year before, which overran most of the country until 1660.
